topics.title: Backup recovery can lose the record of deleted documents
topics.problem: The separate deletion journal can be lost after a backup. Recovery may then stop because a deleted file is missing, or restore a deleted file that remains in the mirror. The repair must cover both cases.
topics.proposedFix: Durably mirror every deletion decision independently of file deletion, and consult that journal even when the old file is still available. Require a trustworthy complete journal before recovery; reconcile snapshot plus later records and verify deleted documents stay unavailable. Merely checking .deleted when a file is missing fails the pending-deletion case.
evidence: Current deletionJournal reads only deletions/ object keys (document-retention.ts:7-9); deletions write object storage17 then DB23 and remove mirror file36. Restore reads current journal15, skips its keys30, and requires every other mirror file32.

Contrary to the absolute historical description, backup.ts:21-35 DOES snapshot document_deletions. But an older snapshot cannot contain later deletions; no independent post-snapshot tombstone mirror is present.

With lost Blob journal and a post-snapshot completed mirror deletion, required file verification aborts before row insertion. If its mirror removal was still pending, absent tombstone information can allow restoration. Source mechanism remains; historical runtime not rerun.

topics.title: Decide retention for never-completed S-election details
topics.problem: Encrypted taxpayer numbers waiting for an EIN have no independent expiry. The approved 14-day clock starts after package delivery, so this is an uncovered pre-delivery policy, not proof the post-delivery promise was broken.

original.truth: The deletion record lives only in Blob storage (storage.ts:57 deletionPath, document-retention.ts:17 putObject) — it is neither in the snapshot (backup.ts:21-36 BACKUP_TABLES and files) nor mirrored to Dropbox. When a client deletes a document after a snapshot, its mirror copy is removed too (document-retention.ts:36). If Blob is then lost, the restore has no journal, treats the deleted file as required, reads no mirror copy and throws at this line, so NOTHING is recovered. Runtime: Restore B (fresh database, empty storage dir, mirror intact) after one post-snapshot deletion → 'Error: Backup file missing or changed: /RB Ein Company, LLC/…EIN Confirmation Letter — RB Ein Company, LLC, PS A.pdf.encrypted', 0 rows in all 14 tables; the same snapshot restores completely when the journal is present (Restore A: 14 tables row-equal, 42/42 files byte-equal) and a snapshot with no later deletion restores from the mirror alone (Restore B0). backup-complete-and-restore.md steps 4-6 and 8. Had the deletion's mirror removal still been pending, the document would instead have been restored as available.
original.replacement: Keep a second copy of every tombstone where the files are: in document-retention.ts requestDocumentDeletion, after `await putObject(path,Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(record)));` add `await uploadMirrorTombstone(record.mirrorPath, record);` (dropbox.ts: write `${path}.deleted` with the record), and in restore.ts replace line 26 onward with: `for(const f of dump.files){if(deleted.has(f.storageKey))continue; const data=await readMirror(f.path); if(!data){const t=await readMirror(f.path+'.deleted'); if(t){const r=JSON.parse(t.toString()) as Deletion; deleted.add(r.storageKey); removedIds.add(r.documentId); continue;}} if(!data||!f.sha||…)throw …}` and re-derive tables.documents after the loop. Also add the deletions journal to the snapshot (`dump.deletions = await deletionJournal()`) so a restore can rebuild it. Update db-restore.md: 'the journal is written to Blob and to Dropbox beside the file'.
